entries.subject: USGS MESSENGER MDIS Basemap BDR global mosaic
entries.finding: The exterior Monochrome view now uses the native USGS BDR GeoTIFF, reduced by pixel-area averaging. The old Trek BDR snapshot is retained only for the interior illustration.

entries.subject: USGS MESSENGER MDIS 665 m enhanced-colour mosaic
entries.finding: The exterior Enhanced color view now uses the native USGS RGB GeoTIFF. Missing polar coverage is gray grid; the former Trek image and modeled completion are retired.

entries.subject: Modelled completion of the enhanced-colour polar no-data pixels
entries.finding: Retired the modeled polar completion. Native enhanced-color observations are reduced directly; missing source footprints are gray grid.
entries.revisitWhen: Do not synthesize missing observations. A future observed product may replace the gaps.

entries.subject: USGS MESSENGER global colour shaded relief (DEM v2 hillshade)
entries.finding: The numeric DEM replaced the colored hillshade in PR #835. Its last remaining use, as a fallback for enhanced-color polar reconstruction, is now retired.
entries.revisitWhen: Use the numeric DEM and its matching scale; the old colored hillshade is not a numeric elevation input.

entries.subject: NASA Science Mercury facts for the interior cutaway
entries.finding: The Interior view and the retained 3D cutaway use the NASA Science facts record retrieved 2026-08-30; the only radial boundary claimed is the 0.85-radius metallic core, mantle and crust stay one combined shell, and colours and fine texture are illustrative.

entries.subject: Outer-shell thickness from the published radii
entries.finding: The rendered 366 km shell is the arithmetic difference between NASA's published 2,440 km planet radius and 2,074 km core radius, while the same source separately describes the shell as about 400 km.
entries.revisitWhen: NASA or another authority publishes radii and a shell thickness that agree.

entries.subject: DLR/Zenodo MESSENGER MASCS one-degree spectral cube
entries.finding: The Spectrum panel is a 326-point, 350-1000 nm global area-weighted mean prepared from M. D'Amore's MASCS cube; the committed snapshot records the 197,099,868-byte archive identity, the aggregation rule, parsed counts and an archive/record count discrepancy.

entries.subject: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature centre points
entries.finding: Named features use the Mercury centre-point export, snapshot 2026-09-11, whose FGDC metadata declares public-domain use: 573 IAU-adopted names with centre, diameter, extent and name origin, labelled at the closest zoom only.

entries.subject: Klimczak, Byrne and Crane global tectonic map, version 2
entries.finding: Feature traces come from the CC BY 4.0 Combined_Tectonic_Map shapefile of 18,451 polylines; the up-to-six longest contractional or extensional structures inside each rupes, dorsum or fossae extent draw that feature's outline.

entries.subject: Feature outlines as published boundaries
entries.finding: The README records that the drawn outlines are not published nomenclature boundaries: craters and faculae trace their published diameter as a circle and other classes trace the Gazetteer extent box or mapped tectonic traces.
entries.revisitWhen: A released dataset supplies mapped nomenclature boundaries for Mercury's features.

entries.subject: Spacecraft landing, touchdown and impact sites
entries.finding: One site is labelled beside the IAU names, each coordinate quoting the NASA NSSDCA, PDS, LROC, agency or paper page it was read from with the stated latitude kind and longitude convention.

entries.subject: English Wikipedia lead summaries as caption notes
entries.finding: 486 labelled names carry a caption note taken from the CC BY-SA 4.0 Wikipedia lead summary retrieved 2026-09-12, joined through Wikidata's Gazetteer id property and pinned with the article link and revision.

entries.subject: NASA/JHU APL/Carnegie MESSENGER global view PIA15162
entries.finding: The navigation marker uses this published MESSENGER global view.

entries.subject: NASA GSFC Planetary Spectrum Generator atmosphere structure
entries.finding: The pinned PSG configuration reports ATMOSPHERE-STRUCTURE as None, so the package deliberately publishes no temperature-pressure chart and describes the thin exosphere separately.
entries.revisitWhen: A source that supplies a usable exosphere structure for Mercury is pinned.

entries.subject: Photometric law for the lighting overlays
entries.finding: Kaasalainen-Shkuratov KS3 at 748.7 nm (Domingue et al. 2016, eq. 43, Table 9), the correction of MESSENGER's final map products, relative to the flood-lit disc centre.

entries.subject: Shared sphere bank lighting (Lambert with a 0.35 flood floor and 0.05 ambient term, adapted from OpenSpace)
entries.finding: Replaced by the published KS3 law; Mercury now bakes its own bank.
entries.revisitWhen: Nothing: an authored limb is not reopened once a published law exists.

entries.subject: Native numeric USGS products and compact display grids
entries.finding: MESSENGER DEM v2 replaces the colored topography input. Native DN uses 0.5 m per unit; central-meridian 180 placement checked against independent native bytes.

entries.subject: Native USGS BDR, LOI and enhanced-color GeoTIFFs, edition 1 (2016)
entries.finding: BDR and LOI share the Monochrome arrow selector. All three maps use native area means at the existing 4K display size. Publisher display stretches are retained and qualified separately. Enhanced-color polar gaps remain missing; no terrain or neighboring hue is used to reconstruct them.

entries.subject: MESSENGER HgM008 free-air gravity anomaly grid, degree 90 (NASA Mercury Trek, Anomaly_Map_HgM008_Lmax90_16ppd)
entries.finding: Adopted as the Gravity lens. The PDS archive holds only the HgM008 coefficients; this numeric GeoTIFF (mGal) was produced by the model's author at NASA Goddard and published by Trek. A sum of the PDS coefficients (degrees 2-90, factor l-1) matches it within 0.15 mGal at 12 cells. The file name says 16ppd; the grid is 0.1 degree. The Trek description calls it a northern orthographic map; the file is a global geographic grid.

entries.subject: Genova et al. (2019) crustal-thickness model from HgM008 and MLA topography (NASA Mercury Trek, CrustalThickness_Map_HgM008_16ppd)
entries.finding: Adopted as the Crust lens and labelled as a model: crust 2,800 kg/m3, crust-mantle contrast 400 kg/m3, mean 35 km, degrees 2-60 with finite-amplitude corrections (paper text and Figure 1 caption). The grid's area-weighted mean is 34.40 km, and 522 cells in Rachmaninoff fall below zero (minimum -3.03 km); both are shown as published. The GeoTIFF declares NaN as no-data, which the shared scientific GeoTIFF reader cannot yet declare; the lens needs that one-line reader change before it can bake.

entries.subject: MESSENGER HgM008 gravity disturbance grid, degree 90 (NASA Mercury Trek, Disturbance_Map_HgM008_Lmax90_16ppd)
entries.finding: Not added. It is the same HgM008 field with degree weighting l+1 instead of l-1 (confirmed within 1.6 mGal by a coefficient sum), so it repeats the Gravity lens with slightly different amplitudes. The paper shows the free-air anomaly. Its georeference stretches 5,762 x 2,881 samples over the globe with identical first and last columns and constant polar rows, which looks like a node grid labelled as cells.
entries.revisitWhen: A reader needs the radial gravity itself rather than the conventional anomaly.

entries.subject: MESSENGER HgM008 degree-strength map (NASA Mercury Trek, DegreeStrength_Map_HgM008_4ppd)
entries.finding: Used as the documented resolution limit of the Gravity and Crust lenses rather than as its own lens: degree 45.6-73.0 north of 60 N and 10.9-15.1 south of 30 S, about 105-125 km versus 500-700 km half-wavelength. A quality mask would need a threshold the product does not publish.

entries.subject: Other Mercury crustal-thickness models (Padovan et al. 2015, Sori 2018, Beuthe et al. 2020)
entries.finding: Not examined for published numeric grids in this change. Each would be an alternative model under its own assumptions, shown beside, not instead of, the Genova et al. (2019) grid.
entries.revisitWhen: A published numeric grid of one of these models is found.
